summary: Independent security and QA review found two high-severity trust/lifecycle defects and two material executable-test gaps. The publisher can proceed from an in-progress verifier, and pending-tag recovery lacks proof that Automatic Release created the tag.
validation: Local release-flow, repository validation, actionlint, and diff checks pass but do not exercise the reported lifecycle/API cases.
Planner chore/fix pending-v0.6.13 coverage and explicit legacy provenance opt-in are present.
blockers: Publisher accepts an in-progress verifier and overwrites its conclusion with success.
Ancestor-tag resumption does not require an exact Automatic Release coordinator proof.
Exact-CI selection and verifier terminal-state behavior need executable policy/API fixtures.
next_action: Require terminal successful verifier state before publication, authenticate resumed tags with exact coordinator proof, and add focused executable negative tests before re-review.

issues.title: Publisher accepts in-progress verifier as successful
issues.details: .github/workflows/publish-release.yaml verifierStateValid permits in_progress and later constructs a verifier object with conclusion success. Poll the exact run to completed success before downloads or writes; fail on cancellation, failure, or timeout.

issues.title: Unproven reachable tags can be auto-published
issues.details: release-plan.py resumes any reachable unpublished stable tag. Require an exact Automatic Release coordinator check/external ID binding tag, source, and successful CI before resumption; reject manually-created tags.

issues.title: Exact CI resolver lacks executable API coverage
issues.details: Add a pure or mocked resolver fixture for exact successful CI selection, zero/duplicate matches, wrong workflow/event/branch/SHA/repository, and rerun attempt selection.

issues.title: Verifier terminal states and attempts lack executable coverage
issues.details: Add policy fixtures for queued/in-progress polling, completed success, failure/cancellation/timeout, attempt mismatch, and stale artifact attempts.
